env.name: cmv
env.description:
Measure the supplied hypotheses; do not discover, rewrite or refine them. Each feature is
one scalar measurement of a discussion row, not a separate observation for every comment.
The full supplied corpus contains 2,000 rows: 1,000 changed and 1,000 unchanged outcomes.
Describe associations, not proven causal effects or prospective prediction.

Columns:
  - post_created_utc: Unix timestamp for the original post, not a comment or score-measurement
    timestamp. Response delay cannot be calculated from it.
  - title: the original poster's (OP's) heading or claim statement, not the argument body.
  - argument: the OP's explanation of their view. Use this field for argument-body measurements;
    include title only when the requested scope includes the heading or when it is needed to
    interpret a comment's target. Text can contain quotations, edits and outcome announcements.
  - OC_comments: a JSON-encoded list of available counter-argument comments by OTHER users,
    not the OP. Parse the list before counting comments, words or semantic instances.
    Specify any/all/count/share/mean explicitly. List order is not rank, importance or chronology.
    If properties must coexist in one comment, assess their conjunction within that comment;
    separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. The row-level extractor still returns one scalar.
    List length counts comments, not necessarily distinct commenters. No per-comment outcomes,
    scores or timestamps are supplied. OP-language measurements use title/argument instead.
  - conversation: formatted interaction text overlapping OC_comments, not extra independent
    evidence. It may include later replies and explicit view-change announcements. Do not use
    it as an initial-argument snapshot. When interaction is required, specify speaker/turn
    selection. Disclose unknown reply timing and do not infer reply links from speaker order alone.
  - log_length: a supplied log-transformed length measure. Construction, source text, log base
    and timing are undocumented. When named by the hypothesis, use the supplied value and state
    that limitation; do not equate it with argument word count or reconstruct its log base.
  - post_score: the observed original-post score, not a comment score, voter count or initial
    endorsement. Its measurement time relative to the outcome is unknown; post_created_utc
    does not establish that timing.
  - delta: OUTCOME, 1 if the OP changed their view, else 0. Never a predictor or annotation input.
  - post_id, comment_id: identifiers, never predictors.

Attribution and unavailable measurements:
  - No measured personality scores, Big Five questionnaires or author demographics are supplied.
    A personality inference from writing is a linguistic proxy, not an observed trait; do not
    substitute it silently when the hypothesis requires an unavailable measurement.
  - Distinguish the author's own assertions or experiences from attributed quotations.
    An external source cited as support can count for an evidence feature without making the
    source's wording or experience the author's own. Background/rebuttal quotations are not
    automatically adopted support. Apply this distinction to OP text and other users' comments.
    Quotation marks alone do not establish another speaker.

Computation and source suitability:
  - Use code for raw counts, regex/literal matching, supplied numeric columns and fixed
    computational recipes. Use a prompt when the measurement requires understanding meaning.
    Do not add semantic filtering to a raw count or URL detector merely because outcome text
    may occur in its source. Disclose that contamination risk; raw text is not outcome-free.
  - Semantic feature specs must exclude OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome
    resolution updates and reports of the outcome as evidence of the construct. Generic
    platform/delta-rule discussion remains eligible. Explicitly requested semantic exclusions
    remain part of any measurement; never remove one just to force code.
  - Use current supplied text unless the hypothesis restricts time. Deleting edits does not
    recover initial/pre-outcome text. No supplied comment/edit timestamps establish timing.
    If a required temporal measurement is unavailable, explain it and set term=null.
  - delta remains the fixed outcome. A hypothesis requiring a different outcome or an
    outcome-revealing predictor is unsupported: preserve the claim, explain it and set
    term=null rather than substituting another test or a cleaned concession/attitude proxy.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument includes explicit comparisons to established scientific or historical norms are associated with lower view change than those without such comparisons.

features.name: argument_compares_to_science_history_norms
features.definition: Does the original argument explicitly compare the OP's view or case to an established scientific or historical norm?
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's own text). Return 1 if the OP's own assertions explicitly compare their view, claim or situation to an established scientific norm/consensus/standard or an established historical norm/precedent (e.g., 'unlike the scientific consensus on X', 'as in historical practice of Y'). Return 0 if no such explicit comparison exists. A mere mention of science or history without comparison does not count. Quoted material counts only if the OP adopts it as their own comparison. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Missing or malformed argument: null.

decomposed.h0: Mean delta does not differ by argument_compares_to_science_history_norms.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with argument_compares_to_science_history_norms=1 have lower view change (delta) than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: 'established norms' is judged by the annotator from the OP's text; no list of norms is supplied. Argument text is current text and may contain edits or outcome announcements, which the prompt excludes as evidence. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Arguments expressing explicit fear of social rejection or isolation are associated with lower view-change rates than arguments stating beliefs without emotional self-defense.

features.name: op_expresses_fear_of_rejection_or_isolation
features.definition: Does the OP's argument explicitly express the OP's own fear of social rejection or isolation?
features.spec: Read only the argument text (OP's body). Return 1 if the OP, in their own assertions (not merely quoted others' words unless adopted), explicitly states fear, worry or dread of being rejected, ostracized, excluded, abandoned, disliked by others, or isolated/lonely as a consequence of their view or of changing it. Return 0 otherwise, including when the OP merely states beliefs. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits or reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty or missing argument gives null.

decomposed.h0: Among arguments, op_expresses_fear_of_rejection_or_isolation is not associated with the view-change (delta) rate.
decomposed.h1: Arguments with op_expresses_fear_of_rejection_or_isolation=1 have lower view-change rates than those without.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: the comparison group is all arguments lacking explicit fear of rejection/isolation (including those stating beliefs plainly); "emotional self-defense" is not separately measured, so the contrast is fear vs. not-fear rather than fear vs. belief-only without any emotion. Argument text is current and may contain edits or outcome announcements (excluded from the semantic judgment, but the text is not guaranteed pre-outcome). Association only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments that cite specific, functioning institutional precedents are associated with a higher probability of view change than those relying on abstract normative principles.

features.name: institutional_precedent_comment_share
features.definition: What share of the counter-argument comments cite a specific, functioning institutional precedent (a real, named policy, law, organization or jurisdiction that actually operates or has operated) as support?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by other users. For each comment decide whether the commenter themself cites at least one specific, real institutional precedent that is functioning/in operation (e.g., a named law, policy, program, court practice, or country/state/organization whose arrangement works in practice) as support for their counter-argument. Purely hypothetical institutions, vague generalities ('some countries'), and abstract principles alone do not count. Quotations of others count only if the commenter adopts them as support. Ignore any statements about the OP changing their view, delta awards, or outcome reports; generic delta-rule discussion is neither evidence nor excluded as topic. Output = number of qualifying comments / total comments (0 to 1). Empty list -> null; missing or malformed -> null. Comment order is not meaningful.

features.name: abstract_principle_comment_share
features.definition: What share of the counter-argument comments rely on abstract normative principles (e.g., fairness, rights, morality) rather than specific institutional precedents?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by other users. For each comment decide whether its counter-argument relies mainly on abstract normative principles or values (e.g., fairness, liberty, rights, justice, what 'ought' to be) stated in general terms, without resting on a specific, real, functioning institutional precedent. Comments citing a specific functioning institutional precedent as their main support do not count; comments with neither (e.g., purely factual or personal anecdote) do not count. Ignore any statements about the OP changing their view, delta awards, or outcome reports. Output = number of qualifying comments / total comments (0 to 1). Empty list -> null; missing or malformed -> null. Comment order is not meaningful.

decomposed.h0: Holding abstract_principle_comment_share fixed, institutional_precedent_comment_share has no association with the probability of view change.
decomposed.h1: Higher institutional_precedent_comment_share is associated with a higher probability of view change, relative to abstract_principle_comment_share.
decomposed.note: Both named groups are measured as shares of a row's comments. The contrast (beta_precedent - beta_principle) is not directly expressible as a single term in this OLS; the tested term is the precedent coefficient with the principle share as covariate. Comments can fall in neither group. Shares are per comment, not per distinct commenter; no chronology or per-comment outcomes are available. OC_comments text may contain outcome announcements (excluded from semantic judgment). 'Functioning' is judged from the comment text alone; no external verification. Association only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring longer precomputed log-transformed discussion length are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: supplied_log_length
features.definition: What is the supplied log-transformed length value for the discussion?
features.spec: Use the supplied log_length column as is: pd.to_numeric(df['log_length'], errors='coerce'). Missing or non-numeric values give null. Do not recompute, rescale or change the log base.

decomposed.h0: supplied_log_length has no association with the likelihood that the OP changed their view (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: Higher supplied_log_length is associated with a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: log_length is used as supplied; its construction, source text, log base and timing are undocumented. It is not equated with argument word count and was not reconstructed. It may include later text or outcome announcements, so contamination/timing risk exists. The association is descriptive, not causal. The OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains explicit admissions of uncertainty are associated with a higher probability of view change than those asserting absolute certainty.

features.name: op_admits_uncertainty
features.definition: Does the original argument contain an explicit admission by the OP of their own uncertainty about their view or claims?
features.spec: Read only `argument` (OP's body text). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly admits uncertainty, doubt, or fallibility about their view or claims (e.g., 'I'm not sure', 'I might be wrong', 'I'm unsure whether'). Return 0 otherwise. Do not count uncertainty merely in quoted other-speaker text unless the OP adopts it, generic hedging words not about the OP's own stance, or any OP view-change/delta-award announcement, post-outcome edit/update, or report of the outcome. Empty text gives 0; missing or malformed gives null.

features.name: op_asserts_absolute_certainty
features.definition: Does the original argument assert absolute certainty about the OP's view, such as claiming it cannot possibly be wrong?
features.spec: Read only `argument`. Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly asserts absolute certainty or infallibility about their view (e.g., 'I am 100% certain', 'there is no possible way I'm wrong', 'undeniably true'). Return 0 otherwise. Do not count quoted other-speaker text unless adopted, ordinary confident statements without explicit absolute-certainty claims, or any OP view-change/delta-award announcement, post-outcome update, or outcome report. Empty text gives 0; missing or malformed gives null.

decomposed.h0: op_admits_uncertainty has no association with the probability of view change, controlling for op_asserts_absolute_certainty.
decomposed.h1: op_admits_uncertainty is associated with a higher probability of view change than op_asserts_absolute_certainty cases, i.e., its coefficient is positive.
decomposed.note: The contrast is operationalized with two separate indicators; the coefficient on op_admits_uncertainty is relative to rows with neither, and does not equal the difference between the two coefficients. Both can be 1 or 0 in a row. Argument text is current text and may include edits or outcome announcements (contamination/timing risk); the semantic features exclude those. Associations only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments frequently challenging multiple distinct factual premises within the argument are positively associated with view change.

features.name: distinct_factual_premises_challenged
features.definition: How many distinct factual premises stated in the OP's argument are challenged by the counter-argument comments?
features.spec: Read argument (OP text) and OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments; parse it). Identify factual premises in the argument: empirical or descriptive claims about the world that could be true or false (not pure value judgments or preferences). Count the distinct such premises that are explicitly challenged (disputed, contradicted, or shown by counter-evidence to be false or unsupported) by at least one comment's own assertions. A premise challenged by several comments counts once; separate premises count separately. Do not count challenges to values, logic only, or non-factual claims; do not count mere quotations of the OP unless the commenter disputes the premise. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates, and reports of the outcome. Output a non-negative integer. If OC_comments is a valid empty list, output 0. If argument or OC_comments is missing or malformed, output null.

decomposed.h0: distinct_factual_premises_challenged has no association with view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher distinct_factual_premises_challenged is positively associated with view change (delta).
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: "frequently challenging multiple distinct factual premises" is measured as the count of distinct OP factual premises challenged across all comments in the row (list order carries no chronology; comments may come from the same commenter). No threshold of "multiple" is imposed; the count is used linearly. Premise identification is a semantic judgment. Argument and comments are current text, may contain edits or outcome announcements, which the prompt excludes; the timing of replies relative to the outcome is unknown. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument contains fewer counter-argument responses are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: counter_argument_count
features.definition: How many counter-argument comments are in the discussion's available list?
features.spec: import json; parse df['OC_comments'] as a JSON list; return len(list). Return null if missing or not parseable as a list; empty list gives 0. Counts comments, not distinct commenters.

decomposed.h0: counter_argument_count has no association with the likelihood that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.h1: Higher counter_argument_count is associated with a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view (fewer responses, lower likelihood).
decomposed.note: "Fewer" is operationalized as a lower count of comments in OC_comments, tested linearly. The supplied list is "available" comments and may be a filtered subset of all replies. It may include comments that led to or followed a delta, so the count could be tied to the outcome. List length counts comments, not distinct commenters. This is an association only. The hypothesis says "original argument contains" responses; the responses come from OC_comments, not the argument text.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions with at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: distinct_counterargument_count
features.definition: How many distinct counter-arguments against the OP's view are made across the posted comments?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by other users. Count the number of distinct counter-arguments (separate reasons, points or lines of reasoning that challenge the OP's view) across all comments. Repeated or paraphrased versions of the same point count once; one comment may contribute several distinct counter-arguments; comments that only ask questions, agree, joke or are off-topic contribute none. Do not count OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates, or reports of the outcome as counter-arguments. Return a non-negative integer. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.

features.name: has_three_plus_counterarguments
features.definition: Are there at least three distinct counter-arguments in the posted comments?
features.spec: Using `distinct_counterargument_count`: df['has_three_plus_counterarguments'] = (df['distinct_counterargument_count'] >= 3).astype(float), with null where df['distinct_counterargument_count'] is null. Yields 1 if count >= 3, else 0.

decomposed.h0: has_three_plus_counterarguments has no association with the likelihood that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with has_three_plus_counterarguments = 1 have a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumptions: "distinct counter-argument" is judged by an LLM as a separate reason challenging the OP's view, deduplicating paraphrases; threshold of 3 as stated. Only OC_comments is used (the supplied available comments, possibly incomplete; list order is not chronology). Comments may contain quoted text or outcome-related remarks; the prompt excludes outcome announcements, but the comment set may still be influenced by the outcome (e.g., comments retained after a delta). OLS on a binary outcome gives a linear probability model; association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original post title uses absolute certainty markers are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: title_absolute_certainty_marker
features.definition: Does the original post title use absolute certainty markers (e.g., always, never, everyone, no one, obviously, undeniably, definitely, 100%)?
features.spec: Read only the title. Return 1 if the title itself asserts with absolute certainty markers, such as universal/absolute quantifiers or intensifiers (always, never, all, every, everyone, no one, nobody, absolutely, obviously, undeniably, definitely, certainly, without a doubt, 100%, completely, impossible). Return 0 if no such marker appears. Ignore hedged uses (e.g., 'I think', 'maybe') only if the marker is not itself asserted as absolute; do not count markers in quoted words attributed to others. Ignore any text announcing view changes or delta awards (not expected in title). Return null if the title is missing or empty.

decomposed.h0: title_absolute_certainty_marker has no association with the likelihood of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.h1: Titles with title_absolute_certainty_marker=1 are associated with a lower likelihood of the OP changing their view than titles without.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: absolute certainty markers are defined by the listed examples (absolute quantifiers and certainty adverbs) with LLM judgment; the list is not exhaustive. Title only is used. Association only, not causal. Titles may rarely contain edits or outcome text, a contamination risk.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where original posts explicitly invite critique or use tentative language are associated with higher view-change rates than those using absolute, definitive declarations.

features.name: op_invites_critique_or_tentative
features.definition: Does the original post explicitly invite critique or use tentative, hedged language about its own view?
features.spec: Read title and argument (OP's own words). Return 1 if the OP explicitly invites challenge/critique/counterarguments (e.g. 'change my view', 'tell me why I'm wrong') beyond the bare 'CMV' title prefix, or states their own view tentatively (e.g. 'I think maybe', 'I'm not sure', 'it seems to me', 'might'). Otherwise 0. Only OP's own assertions count; quoted text from others does not unless adopted. Ignore view-change/delta-award announcements, edits reporting outcomes, and post-outcome updates. Empty/missing title and argument: null.

features.name: op_uses_absolute_declarations
features.definition: Does the original post state its view using absolute, definitive declarations?
features.spec: Read title and argument (OP's own words). Return 1 if the OP asserts their central view in absolute/definitive terms (e.g. 'always', 'never', 'all', 'obviously', 'undeniably', 'without a doubt', flat categorical claims) without hedging. Otherwise 0. Only OP's own assertions count; quotations of others do not unless adopted. Ignore view-change/delta-award announcements, edits reporting outcomes, and post-outcome updates. Empty/missing title and argument: null.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with op_invites_critique_or_tentative=1 have the same view-change rate as others, holding op_uses_absolute_declarations constant.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with op_invites_critique_or_tentative=1 have a higher view-change rate than those with op_uses_absolute_declarations=1.
decomposed.note: Two separate binary measures preserve both named groups; they can overlap or both be 0. The contrast (beta_tentative minus beta_absolute) is not directly expressed by the chosen term, which tests only the tentative/invite coefficient with absolute held constant. Text is current supplied text and may contain edits or outcome announcements; the prompts exclude those, but timing is unknown. Associations only. 'Change my view' title convention is excluded as a generic invitation.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that explicitly cite specific real-world examples are associated with higher likelihood of original view change.

features.name: any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly cite a specific real-world example (a named or concretely identifiable real case, event, person, study or situation) as support?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly cites a specific, concrete real-world example (e.g., a named or identifiable real event, person, organization, place, study, statistic from a particular source, or a concretely described real case) in support of its argument; return 0 if none does (generic claims, hypotheticals, and vague 'some people' statements do not count). A cited external example counts as support even if the commenter did not experience it. Ignore any text that announces the OP's view change, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates, and do not treat them as examples. Use only OC_comments. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.

decomposed.h0: There is no association between any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example and the likelihood of OP view change.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_cites_specific_real_world_example equal to 1 have a higher likelihood of OP view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operationalized "featuring" as at least one counter-comment citing a specific real-world example (any, not share/count). Comment order/timing unknown; comments may contain outcome-related text, which is excluded from the semantic judgment. Association only, not causal. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counterarguments containing measured, logical reasoning are positively associated with the original poster changing their mind compared to those containing emotional aggression in ChangeMyView discussions.

features.name: share_measured_logical_comments
features.definition: What proportion of the counterargument comments present measured, logical reasoning (calm, reasoned argument with premises or evidence leading to conclusions)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by other users. For each comment decide whether the comment's own assertions present measured, logical reasoning: calm, civil, reasoned argumentation with explicit premises, evidence or inference supporting a point. Quoted text from others counts only if adopted by the commenter. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. A comment may satisfy both this and emotional aggression; judge each independently. Return the number of qualifying comments divided by total comments (0 to 1). Empty list: null. Malformed/missing: null.

features.name: share_emotionally_aggressive_comments
features.definition: What proportion of the counterargument comments contain emotional aggression (hostile, angry, insulting or belittling language toward the OP or their view)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by other users. For each comment decide whether the commenter's own text contains emotional aggression: angry, hostile, insulting, contemptuous or belittling language directed at the OP or their view. Mere disagreement or blunt but civil criticism does not count; quoted hostile text counts only if adopted by the commenter. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Judge independently of logical reasoning. Return number of qualifying comments divided by total comments (0 to 1). Empty list: null. Malformed/missing: null.

decomposed.h0: Holding share_emotionally_aggressive_comments constant, share_measured_logical_comments has no association with the OP changing their view.
decomposed.h1: Holding share_emotionally_aggressive_comments constant, higher share_measured_logical_comments is associated with a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.note: The claimed comparison (logical vs aggressive) is operationalized as two separate row-level shares entered together; the exact contrast beta_logical - beta_aggressive is not directly tested by the single term, and the aggressive coefficient should be expected negative. Comments are unordered and without timing; rows with empty comment lists get null. Comment text may contain outcome/delta announcements, excluded in the semantic prompts but contamination risk remains. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote and refute specific factual claims in the original post are associated with higher rates of view change.

features.name: quote_and_refute_op_factual_claim
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly quote or closely reproduce a specific factual claim from the OP's argument and, in that same comment, refute it?
features.spec: Read argument (OP text) and OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users; parse it). Return 1 if at least one single comment both (a) explicitly quotes (verbatim or near-verbatim, e.g. block quote or quotation marks) a specific factual claim that appears in the OP's argument, and (b) in that same comment argues that this factual claim is false, inaccurate or unsupported. Both must occur within the same comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Quoting opinions/value judgments or refuting without quoting gives no credit. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates, and reports of the outcome as evidence. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if OC_comments or argument is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: quote_and_refute_op_factual_claim has no association with the probability of view change.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with quote_and_refute_op_factual_claim = 1 have a higher rate of view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumptions: "specific factual claim" is judged by the annotator; quoting includes near-verbatim reproduction. Comments are unordered and may be after-the-fact; OP argument text may include edits or outcome announcements (excluded from semantic judgment). Association only, tested via OLS linear probability on delta.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly validate the original poster's personal dignity or effort before introducing corrective logic are associated with higher view-change rates than purely logical refutations.

features.name: any_validation_before_correction
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly validate the OP's personal dignity or effort before introducing corrective logic in that same comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one single comment both (a) explicitly validates the OP's personal dignity, worth, or effort (e.g., praising their effort, thoughtfulness, or respecting them as a person; not merely agreeing with an argument point or generic politeness) and (b) afterwards, in that same comment, introduces corrective/counter logic against the OP's view. Validation must precede the corrective logic within the comment. Separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Only the commenter's own assertions count, not quoted text unless adopted. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates, or reports of the outcome as evidence. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with any_validation_before_correction=1 have the same view-change rate as those without it.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_validation_before_correction=1 have a higher view-change rate than those without it.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: the comparison group "purely logical refutations" is operationalized as discussions lacking any comment with validation-before-correction (includes discussions with no corrective logic or with non-qualifying validation). Comment order/timing within list is unknown; "before" is within-comment text order only. OC_comments text may contain outcome announcements or delta-related text; these are excluded from the semantic judgment, but contamination risk remains. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions featuring counter-arguments that provide concrete real-world examples are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those relying primarily on abstract reasoning.

features.name: share_comments_with_concrete_example
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments provide a concrete real-world example (specific case, event, person, data point or personal experience) as support?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). For each comment decide whether it offers at least one concrete real-world example (specific named or described real case, event, person, institution, statistic or firsthand experience) as support for its point, as opposed to purely abstract/general reasoning or hypotheticals. Return the number of such comments divided by the total number of comments (0 to 1). Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Quotations from others count only if cited as an example supporting the commenter's point. Empty list: null. Missing or malformed input: null.

decomposed.h0: share_comments_with_concrete_example has no association with the likelihood of view change.
decomposed.h1: Higher share_comments_with_concrete_example is associated with a higher likelihood of view change.
decomposed.note: Operationalization: "relying primarily on abstract reasoning" is treated as the low end of the share of comments with concrete examples; a continuous share is used rather than a majority-based dichotomy. Comments are unordered, with no timing; OC_comments may contain outcome-related text, which is excluded semantically. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly engage with the specific examples or premises cited in the original argument text are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.

features.name: share_comments_engaging_op_examples_premises
features.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments explicitly engage with a specific example or premise cited in the OP's argument text?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). For each comment, decide whether it explicitly engages (addresses, rebuts, questions, or builds on by specific reference) a particular example or premise stated in the OP's argument text, rather than only giving generic or unrelated points. Read argument to identify the OP's examples/premises. Count only the commenter's own engagement; ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_quotes_and_refutes_op_phrase = 1 have a higher likelihood of view change (delta) than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operationalized as at least one comment (any, not share) with quote and refutation in the same comment. Comment order/timing unknown. OC_comments and the OP text may contain outcome announcements; semantic spec excludes them. Association only. OP text is current, possibly edited. Quotes counted only if from OP text.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly refute specific examples or anecdotes provided by the original poster are associated with a higher probability of view change compared to arguments addressing the main premise directly.

features.name: any_comment_refutes_op_example
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly refute a specific example or anecdote that the original poster gave in their argument?
features.spec: Read argument (OP text) and OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertions, explicitly disputes, rebuts or debunks a specific example, case or anecdote that the OP provided in argument (e.g., argues the OP's cited case is factually wrong or does not show what OP claims). Return 0 if no comment does so, including when comments only address the general premise. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Quoted text counts only if the commenter adopts the refutation. Empty comment list: 0. Missing/malformed input: null.

features.name: any_comment_addresses_main_premise
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment directly argue against the OP's main premise or overall claim rather than a specific example?
features.spec: Read title and argument (OP's main claim) and OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments; parse it). Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertions, directly argues against the OP's central premise/general claim (not merely a specific example or anecdote). Return 0 otherwise. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence. Empty comment list: 0. Missing/malformed input: null.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_refutes_op_example has no association with the probability of view change, controlling for any_comment_addresses_main_premise.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_refutes_op_example=1 have a higher probability of view change than those without, controlling for any_comment_addresses_main_premise.
decomposed.note: The hypothesis compares example-refuting vs main-premise-addressing arguments; the OLS contrast beta_example - beta_premise is not directly a single term, so the example coefficient is tested with premise held fixed (approximation). Features are not mutually exclusive; both can be 1. List order gives no chronology; no reply links inferred. Comment text and conversation may contain outcome announcements; semantic features exclude them, but residual contamination is possible. Associations only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument uses hedging or qualifying language are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those using absolute declarative statements.

features.name: argument_hedging_share
features.definition: What proportion of the OP's own assertive sentences in the argument use hedging or qualifying language rather than absolute declarative phrasing?
features.spec: Read only the argument text (OP's body). Consider the OP's own declarative claims/assertions (ignore questions, quotations of others not adopted by the OP, and any view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits or reports of the outcome). Count claims that use hedging/qualifying language (e.g., 'might', 'perhaps', 'I think', 'in some cases', 'generally', 'tend to', 'seems') as hedged; claims stated flatly or absolutely (e.g., 'always', 'never', 'obviously', unqualified 'X is Y') as absolute. Return hedged / (hedged + absolute) as a number in [0,1]. If argument is missing or malformed return null; if there are no eligible claims return null.

decomposed.h0: argument_hedging_share has no association with the likelihood of view change.
decomposed.h1: Higher argument_hedging_share is associated with a higher likelihood of view change.
decomposed.note: Operationalized as a continuous share of hedged vs absolute claims in the OP's argument; the hedged-vs-absolute comparison is a continuum, not two separate groups. Current argument text may include edits or outcome announcements (the prompt excludes them semantically, but edit timing is unknown). OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly quote the original poster's text rather than paraphrasing are associated with a higher probability of view change.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_op
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly quote the OP's own title or argument wording?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly quotes the OP's wording from title or argument (verbatim or near-verbatim text, e.g. in quotation marks or blockquote '>' lines, matching OP's text). Return 0 if no comment does so (including empty list). Quotes of other sources or other users do not count. Paraphrase without reproducing OP wording does not count. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements or outcome reports as evidence. Missing or malformed OC_comments, title or argument: null.

features.name: any_comment_paraphrases_op
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment restate the OP's view in its own words without quoting the OP's wording?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly restates or summarizes the OP's claim/argument from title or argument in its own words (paraphrase, not reproducing OP wording in quotes or blockquote). Return 0 if none does (including empty list). Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements or outcome reports as evidence. Missing or malformed inputs: null.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_quotes_op is not associated with probability of view change (delta) when controlling for any_comment_paraphrases_op.
decomposed.h1: any_comment_quotes_op is associated with a higher probability of view change than its absence, controlling for any_comment_paraphrases_op.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: "quote rather than paraphrase" is measured at discussion level as presence of quoting, with paraphrase presence as a covariate; the coefficient is not an exact quote-vs-paraphrase contrast (overlap and neither cases preserved). Quoting is judged against current title/argument, which may include edits or outcome announcements (excluded semantically). Comment order and timing unknown; OC_comments may include comments after the view change. Associations only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that explicitly validate the original poster's emotional experience prior to logical rebuttal are associated with higher view-change rates.

features.name: any_comment_validates_emotion_before_rebuttal
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly validate the original poster's emotional experience before giving its logical rebuttal within that same comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Return 1 if at least one single comment both (a) explicitly acknowledges or validates the OP's feelings or emotional experience (e.g., 'I understand why you feel frustrated', 'that sounds painful') in the commenter's own words, and (b) afterwards in that same comment gives a logical rebuttal or counter-argument to the OP's view; the validation must come earlier in the comment than the rebuttal. Separate comments cannot jointly satisfy this. Do not count validation only of the OP's reasoning or effort without emotion, validation appearing after the rebuttal, or merely quoted emotional wording not adopted by the commenter. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, outcome reports, and post-outcome resolution text as evidence. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_validates_emotion_before_rebuttal has no association with the probability of OP view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_validates_emotion_before_rebuttal = 1 have a higher view-change rate than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: 'discussions containing' means at least one such comment. Order is assessed within a single comment's text only; no chronology across comments is available. OC_comments may include text post-dating the outcome, with unknown timing; the semantic spec excludes outcome announcements. Outcome delta is modeled by OLS (linear probability), describing association only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that use analogies to familiar scenarios are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: any_analogy_counterargument
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment use an analogy to a familiar scenario?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of counter-argument comments by other users. Return 1 if at least one comment itself uses an analogy, i.e. compares the OP's issue to a different, familiar everyday or well-known scenario to make its point (e.g. 'it's like when ...'). Return 0 if no comment does so. Count the commenter's own analogies, not analogies merely quoted from others unless the commenter adopts them. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Literal examples of the OP's own topic are not analogies. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.

decomposed.h0: any_analogy_counterargument has no association with the likelihood of the OP changing their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_analogy_counterargument=1 have a higher likelihood of the OP changing their view than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operationalized as presence of at least one analogy-using counter-argument comment; "familiar scenarios" is judged by the annotator. OC_comments may contain text after the outcome and no timing is available, so analogy use may follow or reflect the view change. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the title explicitly contains an absolute universal quantifier like 'all' or 'never' are associated with lower view change than those using variable or probabilistic terms.

features.name: title_has_absolute_quantifier
features.definition: Does the title explicitly contain an absolute universal quantifier such as 'all', 'never', 'always', 'every', 'none' or 'no one'?
features.spec: Read df['title']. If missing/non-string return null. Lowercase and test case-insensitive whole-word regex r"\b(all|never|always|every|everyone|everybody|everything|none|no one|nobody|nothing|no)\b"; return 1 if any match else 0. Raw literal match; no semantic filtering.

features.name: title_has_probabilistic_quantifier
features.definition: Does the title explicitly contain a variable or probabilistic term such as 'some', 'many', 'most', 'often', 'sometimes', 'usually', 'may' or 'might'?
features.spec: Read df['title']. If missing/non-string return null. Lowercase and test case-insensitive whole-word regex r"\b(some|many|most|often|sometimes|usually|generally|typically|rarely|seldom|few|may|might|can|could|probably|likely|unlikely|perhaps|occasionally)\b"; return 1 if any match else 0. Raw literal match; no semantic filtering.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with titles containing absolute universal quantifiers (title_has_absolute_quantifier=1) have the same or higher view-change rate as those without, holding title_has_probabilistic_quantifier constant.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with title_has_absolute_quantifier=1 have lower view-change rate than those with title_has_probabilistic_quantifier=1 and no absolute term.
decomposed.note: Term lists are operational assumptions (not supplied by hypothesis); keyword matching ignores context (e.g. 'no' as determiner, negation, 'can' as noun). Comparison group is titles with probabilistic terms; the model's absolute coefficient compares against titles with neither term plus controls for probabilistic, so it is only an approximation of the absolute-vs-probabilistic contrast. Titles with both terms or neither are possible. Titles are current text; association only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that explicitly reference specific, concrete examples or real-world instances in the provided comments are associated with a higher probability of view change.

features.name: any_comment_cites_concrete_example
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly reference a specific, concrete example or real-world instance?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment itself explicitly refers to a specific, concrete example or real-world instance (e.g., a named person, event, case, place, product, study, or described particular situation) offered in support of its counter-argument. Return 0 if no comment does (only abstract/general reasoning or hypotheticals). Quoted text from others counts only if the commenter cites it as a concrete example in support. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution; these are not evidence. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_cites_concrete_example is not associated with the probability of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_cites_concrete_example = 1 have a higher probability of view change.
decomposed.note: Presence (any comment) is assumed as the operationalization of 'discussions containing' such counter-arguments. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model. Comment text may contain outcome announcements and has unknown timing; the prompt excludes these as evidence. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments contain specific empirical evidence are more likely to be associated with the original poster changing their view than those containing only logical refutations.

features.name: any_comment_specific_empirical_evidence
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment offer specific empirical evidence (e.g., concrete data, statistics, studies, documented facts or cited real-world cases) to support its point?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment itself presents specific empirical evidence as support: concrete statistics, named studies or sources, documented historical/real-world cases or measurable data. Vague appeals to common sense, generic assertions, hypotheticals and purely logical argument do not count. An external source cited as support counts. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view/awarded a delta or reporting the outcome; do not count it as evidence. Generic delta-rule discussion is neutral. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if missing or malformed.

features.name: only_logical_refutation_comments
features.definition: Do the counter-argument comments contain at least one logical refutation (reasoning against the OP's view) and no comment with specific empirical evidence?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment offers a logical refutation (reasoning, conceptual distinctions, internal inconsistency or counter-logic against the OP's view) AND no comment presents specific empirical evidence (concrete statistics, named studies/sources, documented real-world cases or measurable data). Return 0 if the list is empty, has no logical refutation, or any comment contains specific empirical evidence. Ignore text announcing the OP changed their view/awarded a delta or reporting the outcome; it is not evidence of either. Null if missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: Controlling for only_logical_refutation_comments, any_comment_specific_empirical_evidence is unrelated to the probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_specific_empirical_evidence=1 have a higher probability of OP view change than those with only_logical_refutation_comments=1.
decomposed.note: Reference group is neither feature (no empirical evidence and no logical refutation), so the empirical coefficient is relative to that group, not directly versus only-logical; the exact contrast beta_emp - beta_logical is not expressible as a single term. Comment order, timing and per-comment outcomes are unavailable. Comment text may contain delta/view-change announcements, which the prompts are told to ignore. Associations only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly acknowledge the validity of a specific component of the original argument before presenting a counter-example are associated with higher view change rates.

features.name: ack_then_counterexample_comment
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly acknowledge the validity of a specific component of the OP's argument and then, in that same comment, present a counter-example?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Read argument only to identify which OP claims/components a comment refers to. Return 1 if at least one single comment (a) explicitly acknowledges that a specific component, claim or premise of the OP's argument is valid/correct/fair (not mere generic politeness or vague agreement) in its own assertions, and (b) afterwards in that same comment presents a counter-example (a specific case, instance or scenario that contradicts or challenges the OP's view). Both conditions must be met within one comment; separate comments cannot jointly satisfy it. Acknowledgment must be by the commenter, not merely quoted OP text. Ignore any text where the OP announces a view change, awards a delta, or reports the outcome, and post-outcome resolution updates; generic delta-rule discussion is eligible but is not itself evidence. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment qualifies; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: ack_then_counterexample_comment has no association with delta (view change) rate.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with ack_then_counterexample_comment = 1 have a higher view change rate than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Assumes "discussions where counter-arguments..." means at least one comment satisfies the conjunction (any-comment). Association only. OC_comments order carries no chronology; "before" is interpreted within a single comment's text. Comments may contain outcome announcements or delta-related text, which the prompt excludes as evidence. The argument column is used only to identify the OP's components; current text may include edits.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments utilize second-person direct address are associated with higher original poster view-change rates than arguments relying on third-person analysis.

features.name: share_comments_second_person_address
features.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments use second-person direct address to the original poster?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). For each comment decide whether the commenter's own wording directly addresses the reader/OP in the second person (e.g. 'you', 'your', 'you're' referring to the OP or interlocutor, as in 'you say', 'your view'). Generic/impersonal 'you' (meaning 'one'), and second-person wording only inside quotations of others, do not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, outcome reports or post-outcome resolution text. Return number of qualifying comments divided by total comments (0 to 1). Empty list: null. Malformed/missing: null.

features.name: share_comments_third_person_analysis
features.definition: What proportion of counter-argument comments rely on third-person analysis of the issue rather than directly addressing the original poster?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments. For each comment decide whether its argument is framed as third-person analysis of the topic, groups, or arguments (e.g. 'people', 'they', 'the policy', 'one could') WITHOUT second-person direct address to the OP in the commenter's own wording. Comments using direct second-person address to the OP do not count (mixed comments are excluded from this feature). Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, outcome reports or post-outcome resolution text. Return qualifying comments divided by total comments (0 to 1). Empty list: null. Malformed/missing: null.

decomposed.h0: share_comments_second_person_address has no association with view change, controlling for share_comments_third_person_analysis.
decomposed.h1: Higher share_comments_second_person_address is associated with higher OP view-change rates, relative to third-person analysis share.
decomposed.note: Both named groups are measured, but the OLS coefficient on the second-person share (holding third-person share fixed) is not exactly the contrast second-person minus third-person; the two shares exclude mixed comments and are not complements. Comment order/timing unknown; text may contain outcome announcements (excluded from semantic measurement). Association only. Impersonal 'you' is excluded by judgment of the annotator. Discussion-level association, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Original posts with direct personal anecdotes in the argument are associated with a lower probability of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: op_has_personal_anecdote
features.definition: Does the OP's argument text include a direct personal anecdote about the OP's own experience?
features.spec: Read only the `argument` column (OP's text). Return 1 if the OP's own assertions include at least one direct personal anecdote: a specific account of something that happened to or was done/experienced by the OP themself (e.g., 'when I was in school, my teacher...'). Return 0 if there is none: only general claims, hypotheticals, others' experiences, statistics, or quoted/cited sources not adopted as the OP's own experience. Quotation marks alone do not establish another speaker. Ignore view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits/resolution updates and reports of the outcome; they do not count as anecdotes. Missing or malformed argument gives null; empty text gives 0.

decomposed.h0: op_has_personal_anecdote has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Posts with op_has_personal_anecdote = 1 are associated with a lower probability of the OP changing their view than posts with 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: personal anecdote means a specific account of the OP's own experience, judged from the current argument text. The argument may include later edits or outcome announcements, and no timestamps establish timing; the prompt excludes these as evidence. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments explicitly introduce verifiable external facts distinct from the original argument are associated with a higher probability of view change.

features.name: cc_external_facts_present
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly introduce a verifiable external fact that is distinct from what the original argument already states?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than OP). Read argument only to judge whether a fact is distinct from the OP's own argument. Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly introduces a verifiable external fact (e.g., a specific statistic, study, documented event, law, historical or scientific fact, or cited source) that is not already stated in argument; the comment itself must assert it or cite it as support. Return 0 if no comment does (opinions, reasoning, hypotheticals, personal anecdotes that cannot be verified, and facts merely restating the OP do not count). Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates, and reports of the outcome as evidence; generic delta-rule discussion is eligible. Quoted text counts only as cited support, not as the commenter's own assertion unless adopted. Empty or valid empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null. Comment order carries no chronology.

decomposed.h0: cc_external_facts_present has no association with the probability of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with cc_external_facts_present=1 have a higher probability of view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: "discussions where counter-arguments introduce" is measured as any comment introducing such facts. Verifiability is judged from the text alone, with no external checking. Distinctness from the original argument is judged against current argument text, which may include edits or outcome announcements. OC_comments may contain outcome-related content, and reply timing is unknown. The association is not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument explicitly acknowledges the existence of alternative perspectives are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those presenting the argument as singularly deterministic.

features.name: op_acknowledges_alternative_perspectives
features.definition: Does the original argument explicitly acknowledge that alternative perspectives or opposing views exist?
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's own text). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly acknowledges that other perspectives, views, or reasonable disagreement exist (e.g., 'some people think...', 'I know others see it differently', 'I may be wrong, there are other sides'). Return 0 if the argument is presented without such acknowledgment (singularly deterministic framing) or only quotes others without adopting the acknowledgment. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, edits reporting outcomes, or post-outcome updates; do not count them as evidence. Generic mention of platform rules is fine. Missing or malformed argument gives null; empty text gives 0.

decomposed.h0: Discussions whose original argument explicitly acknowledges alternative perspectives have the same likelihood of view change as those that do not (op_acknowledges_alternative_perspectives coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with op_acknowledges_alternative_perspectives = 1 have higher likelihood of view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: the 'singularly deterministic' comparison group is operationalized as the absence of explicit acknowledgment of alternatives (not-A), since no separate deterministic-framing measure was requested. Argument text is current text and may include edits or outcome announcements; the prompt excludes these, but timing relative to the outcome is unknown. Association only, tested with OLS (linear probability model) on delta.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing multiple distinct counter-argument comments are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those containing only a single comment.

features.name: multiple_counter_comments
features.definition: Does the discussion contain more than one counter-argument comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list. Return 1 if len(list) >= 2, 0 if len(list) == 1 (an empty list gives 0). Return null if missing or malformed. Counts list entries, not verified distinct commenters or distinct arguments.

decomposed.h0: multiple_counter_comments has no association with view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with multiple_counter_comments = 1 have a higher likelihood of view change than those with a single comment.
decomposed.note: "Distinct" is operationalized as separate list entries; the list may include multiple comments by the same commenter and no per-comment authorship is supplied. Order and timing are unknown. The comment list may contain outcome announcements or later replies; this is a raw count and not filtered for them. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Counter-arguments frequently embedding direct quotations from the original post are associated with a higher likelihood of view change than those lacking explicit textual anchoring.

features.name: share_comments_quoting_op
features.definition: What proportion of the counter-argument comments directly quote wording from the original post (title or argument)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of comments by other users. For each comment, decide whether it contains a direct quotation (verbatim or near-verbatim wording, e.g. in quote marks or markdown '>' blockquote) of text that appears in the OP's title or argument. Compare against title and argument to verify the quoted text is from the OP, not from another source or another commenter. Quote marks alone do not suffice; the quoted text must match OP wording. Paraphrases without quoted OP wording do not count. Ignore content that only announces OP view change/delta awards or reports the outcome; such content is not evidence of quoting. Output = (comments with an OP quote) / (total comments), in [0,1]. Return null if OC_comments is missing or malformed, or if the list is empty.

decomposed.h0: share_comments_quoting_op has no association with the likelihood of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: A higher share_comments_quoting_op is associated with a higher likelihood of view change.
decomposed.note: Operationalization: "frequently embedding" is measured as the share of comments quoting the OP, a continuous measure rather than a threshold. The "lacking explicit anchoring" comparison corresponds to low values of the share, including 0. Comment order and timing are unknown. OC_comments and the OP text may contain outcome announcements; the quote feature ignores these, but the text sources are not outcome-free. Association only, not causal. Rows with an empty comment list get null.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments with specific real-world examples are associated with a higher probability of original poster view change than those lacking such citations.

features.name: any_oc_specific_real_world_example
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment offer a specific real-world example as support?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment itself cites a specific, concrete real-world example (a named or identifiable real case, event, person, organization, study, place, statistic from a real instance, or concrete personal/real experience) as support for its counter-argument; an external source cited as support counts. Return 0 if the list is valid but no comment does (including only hypotheticals, generic claims, or abstract reasoning), and 0 for a valid empty list. Return null if missing or malformed. Ignore any text announcing OP view change/delta awards, post-outcome resolution updates, or reports of the outcome; these are not evidence of an example. Do not read other columns.

decomposed.h0: any_oc_specific_real_world_example has no association with the probability of OP view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_oc_specific_real_world_example = 1 have a higher probability of OP view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: "discussions containing counter-arguments with specific real-world examples" is measured as at least one counter-argument comment in OC_comments containing such an example. Comment order/timing unknown; associations only, not causal. OC_comments may contain outcome announcements or later replies, which are excluded semantically from the measurement, but timing relative to the OP's decision is unknown. Outcome delta is not used as input.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments with higher lexical density are associated with a lower likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: counterargument_content_word_share
features.definition: What proportion of words across the counterargument comments are content words (nouns, verbs, adjectives or adverbs)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments as a JSON list of strings; missing or malformed -> null. Concatenate all comments (pooled, not per-comment mean). Tokenize into words (alphabetic tokens, e.g. nltk word_tokenize, keeping tokens with at least one letter) and POS-tag with a fixed tagger (e.g. NLTK averaged perceptron, Penn tags). Content words are tags starting with NN, VB, JJ or RB. Value = content-word tokens / total word tokens. Empty list or zero word tokens -> null. Raw text is used as supplied; it may contain outcome announcements and is not filtered.

decomposed.h0: counterargument_content_word_share has no association with the likelihood of the OP changing their view (delta).
decomposed.h1: Higher counterargument_content_word_share is associated with a lower likelihood of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.note: Lexical density is operationalized as the pooled share of content words (NN, VB, JJ, RB POS tags) across all counterargument comments. The tagger and tokenization are assumptions. OC_comments are current text; they may include post-outcome content, and reply timing is unknown. The test is an association only. OLS is used per the contract, so it is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that cite specific, localized examples are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: any_comment_cites_specific_local_example
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment cite a specific, localized example (a particular named or concretely situated case, place, event, person or instance) as support?
