decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions with post creation timestamps later in the dataset period are associated with a higher likelihood of view change.

features.name: post_created_timestamp
features.definition: What is the original post's creation time as a Unix timestamp (later = larger)?
features.spec: df['post_created_timestamp'] = pd.to_numeric(df['post_created_utc'], errors='coerce'); null if missing or malformed. Units: Unix seconds.

decomposed.h0: post_created_timestamp has no association with the likelihood of view change.
decomposed.h1: Higher post_created_timestamp (later posts) is associated with a higher likelihood of view change.
decomposed.note: "Later in the dataset period" is operationalized as a linear trend in the raw Unix timestamp of post creation (range ~2013 to 2025). Only an association is tested, with a linear OLS term; non-linear time trends are not modeled. The timestamp is the OP's post time, not any comment or outcome time. The sample is balanced 1,000 changed and 1,000 unchanged, so the baseline rate is not natural.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing counter-arguments that explicitly quote or reference specific textual elements of the original post are associated with a higher probability of the original poster's view changing.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_or_references_op_text
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment explicitly quote or reference a specific textual element of the original post?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Return 1 if at least one comment explicitly quotes (verbatim or near-verbatim, e.g. block quote or quotation marks matching OP wording) or explicitly points to a specific passage, sentence, phrase, claim or wording of the OP's title or argument (e.g. 'you said X', 'your point about Y in the post'). Use title and argument only to verify that the quoted/referenced element comes from the OP post. Generic references to the OP's overall view without a specific textual element do not count. Quotation marks alone do not suffice if the text is not from the OP post. Ignore OP view-change/delta announcements and post-outcome resolution updates as evidence. Return 0 if no comment qualifies or the list is empty; null if OC_comments is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_quotes_or_references_op_text has no association with the probability of view change (delta).
decomposed.h1: Rows with any_comment_quotes_or_references_op_text = 1 have a higher probability of view change.
decomposed.note: Operationalized as "at least one comment" for "discussions containing" such counter-arguments. Linear probability model on binary delta. Comments may be from after the OP's text was edited; the current text may contain edits or outcome announcements, and comment timing is unknown. Association only.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the counter-arguments contain direct quotations from the original post are associated with a higher probability of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: any_comment_quotes_op
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment directly quote wording from the original post's argument?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Return 1 if at least one comment directly quotes the OP's wording from the argument text (verbatim or near-verbatim excerpt, e.g. in quote marks or blockquote '>' format, that matches a passage in the argument column). Verify the match against argument. Quotation marks alone do not suffice; quoted text from other sources does not count. Quote presence needs no endorsement or refutation. Ignore quoted text that is only an OP view-change/delta announcement or post-outcome update. Return 0 if the list is valid but empty or no comment quotes the OP. Return null if OC_comments or argument is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_quotes_op is unassociated with the probability of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_quotes_op = 1 have a higher probability of the OP changing their view.
decomposed.note: Association only. Operationalized as presence of at least one comment quoting the OP's argument text; title quotes are not included. Current argument text may include edits or outcome announcements, and comment order/timing is unknown. OLS on the binary delta outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: ChangeMyView posters receiving substantive counterarguments demonstrate higher levels of view modification than those receiving only supportive comments.

features.name: any_substantive_counterargument
features.definition: Does at least one comment offer a substantive counterargument, meaning a reasoned challenge to the OP's view with specific reasons, evidence or examples?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertions (not unadopted quotations), gives a substantive counterargument: a reasoned challenge to the OP's position supported by specific reasons, evidence, examples or logic. Return 0 if the list is non-empty and no comment does (e.g., only supportive, off-topic, joking, or bare disagreement with no reasoning). Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null. Ignore any OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome; they are not evidence of substantiveness.

features.name: only_supportive_comments
features.definition: Are all of the comments supportive of the OP's view, with none offering a counterargument?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if the list is non-empty and every comment, in its own assertions (not unadopted quotations), expresses support, agreement or validation of the OP's view, with no comment offering any counterargument or challenge to the OP's view. Return 0 if the list is non-empty and at least one comment is not supportive (counterargument, neutral, off-topic, etc.). Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null. Ignore OP view-change or delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome as evidence.

decomposed.h0: Posters whose rows have any_substantive_counterargument = 1 are no more likely to change their view than those with only_supportive_comments = 1, holding the other indicator fixed.
decomposed.h1: Rows with any_substantive_counterargument = 1 have higher view-change (delta) than rows with only_supportive_comments = 1.
decomposed.note: Both named groups are measured. The groups are not exhaustive: rows with neither indicator (empty comments, or only non-substantive non-supportive comments) form the reference category, so the coefficient on any_substantive_counterargument is a contrast against that reference, not directly against only-supportive rows; the exact difference beta_substantive minus beta_supportive is not a single design-matrix term. 'Higher view modification' is operationalised as the binary delta outcome. OC_comments are described as counter-argument comments, so supportive-only rows may be rare. Comment order and timing are unknown. Comments may contain outcome announcements or delta-related text, which are excluded from semantic judgments; the raw text is not outcome-free. Associations only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions containing specific counter-arguments citing empirical examples are more likely to be associated with original poster view change than those lacking such evidence.

features.name: has_empirical_example_counterargument
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment give a specific empirical example (a concrete real-world case, data, study or statistic) in support of its counter-argument?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment makes a specific counter-argument that cites a concrete empirical example as support: a named or particular real-world case, event, study, statistic, dataset or documented observation (including the commenter's own concrete experience or an external source cited as support). Return 0 if no comment does (only abstract reasoning, generic claims, hypotheticals, or vague appeals). Ignore comments' mentions of OP view change, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates as evidence; generic delta-rule discussion is not evidence either. Purely background quotations of others that are not used as support do not count. Empty list gives 0; missing or unparseable OC_comments gives null.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with a specific empirical-example counter-argument (has_empirical_example_counterargument=1) have the same association with OP view change (delta) as those without.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with has_empirical_example_counterargument=1 are more likely to have OP view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Association only. Operationally, "specific counter-argument citing empirical examples" is assessed as any available comment in OC_comments containing a concrete empirical example. Comment order/timing unknown; comments may contain outcome announcements, which are excluded as evidence in the semantic judgment. The comment list may be incomplete. Comparison group is discussions lacking such comments.

decomposed.hypothesis: Posts where the original poster explicitly requests emotional support or assistance in the argument text are less likely to result in a view change.

features.name: op_requests_emotional_support_or_assistance
features.definition: Does the original poster explicitly request emotional support or assistance in the argument text?
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's text). Return 1 if the OP, in their own words, explicitly asks readers for emotional support (e.g., comfort, reassurance, encouragement) or for assistance/help (e.g., asks for help with their situation or problem). Return 0 if no such explicit request exists; a plain request to 'change my view' alone does not count. Ignore quoted text not adopted by the OP. Exclude view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome updates and reports of the outcome; they are not evidence. Return null if argument is missing or malformed.

decomposed.h0: op_requests_emotional_support_or_assistance has no association with the probability of a view change.
decomposed.h1: Posts with op_requests_emotional_support_or_assistance=1 have a lower probability of a view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Assumption: "assistance" is read as an explicit request for help beyond the standard CMV request to change the view. The argument text is the current text and may contain edits or outcome announcements; the prompt excludes these, but timing is unknown. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments introduce concrete, external factual analogies are associated with higher view-change rates than those relying solely on abstract logical refutation.

features.name: any_concrete_external_analogy
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment introduce a concrete, external factual analogy (a specific real-world case, example or comparison from outside the OP's own scenario) to support its point?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment itself introduces a concrete, external factual analogy: a specific real-world case, event, institution, or parallel situation from outside the OP's own scenario, used as an analogy or comparison to support its argument. Return 0 if comments are valid but none contain such analogies (e.g. purely abstract logical refutation, or only generic statements). Quoting the OP does not count. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, thanks, or post-outcome resolution updates as evidence; generic delta-rule discussion is not evidence either. Empty list -> 0; missing or malformed -> null.

decomposed.h0: any_concrete_external_analogy has no association with view-change (delta) rate.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_concrete_external_analogy = 1 have a higher view-change rate than those without.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: the comparison group "relying solely on abstract logical refutation" is operationalized as discussions with no comment containing a concrete external analogy (feature = 0), which also includes discussions with other non-analogy content. Comment order, timing and per-comment outcomes are unavailable. OC_comments may contain post-outcome text; the prompt excludes such announcements as evidence. Association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original argument exceeds one hundred words are associated with a lower likelihood of view change than shorter arguments.

features.name: argument_over_100_words
features.definition: Does the original argument contain more than one hundred words?
features.spec: If df['argument'] is missing or not a string, return null. Otherwise count words as len(re.findall(r"\S+", argument.strip())) (whitespace-delimited tokens) and return 1 if count > 100 else 0. Empty string gives 0 (count 0). Raw text count; no semantic filtering.

decomposed.h0: Discussions with argument_over_100_words equal to 1 have the same likelihood of view change as those with 0.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with argument_over_100_words equal to 1 have a lower likelihood of view change than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Word count uses whitespace tokens of the current argument text (OP body only, not title). Argument text may include edits or outcome announcements (e.g., delta awards), which are counted as raw words; the text is not outcome-free and its timing is unknown. OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only. The supplied log_length is not used because its construction is undocumented.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where the original post's argument explicitly acknowledges potential counterpoints are associated with a higher likelihood of the view changing.

features.name: op_acknowledges_counterpoints
features.definition: Does the original post's argument explicitly acknowledge potential counterpoints, objections or opposing views to the OP's own position?
features.spec: Read only the argument column (OP's text). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, explicitly acknowledges potential counterpoints, objections, counterarguments or opposing views to their position (e.g., 'some may argue...', 'I know the counterargument is...', 'one objection is...'). Return 0 if no such explicit acknowledgment exists. Quotations of others count only if the OP adopts them as a counterpoint to their own view. Ignore view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits or updates, and reports of the outcome; do not treat them as acknowledgment. Generic platform-rule discussion is eligible but not itself an acknowledgment. Return null if argument is missing or malformed; empty text gives 0.

decomposed.h0: op_acknowledges_counterpoints has no association with the likelihood of the view changing (delta).
decomposed.h1: Discussions with op_acknowledges_counterpoints = 1 have a higher likelihood of the view changing than those with 0.
decomposed.note: Uses current argument text, which may include later edits or outcome announcements; no timestamps establish pre-outcome timing. Explicitness is judged by the prompt without a fixed scale. Association only, not causal. OLS on binary outcome is a linear probability model.

decomposed.hypothesis: Observed discussions with a higher log-transformed length measure are associated with a higher probability that the original poster changes their view.

features.name: supplied_log_length
features.definition: What is the supplied log-transformed length value for the discussion?
features.spec: df['supplied_log_length'] = pd.to_numeric(df['log_length'], errors='coerce'); missing or non-numeric values become null. Use the supplied value as is; do not recompute or rebase.

decomposed.h0: supplied_log_length has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.h1: Higher supplied_log_length is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view.
decomposed.note: log_length is used as supplied; its construction, source text, log base and timing are undocumented. It is not assumed to equal argument word count. It may include text produced after the outcome, so timing and contamination risk exist. The test is a linear OLS association with delta, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: Disclosures of personal emotional vulnerability in the original argument are associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster changing their view.

features.name: op_discloses_emotional_vulnerability
features.definition: Does the original poster, in their own words in the argument, disclose a personal emotional vulnerability (e.g., their own fear, shame, insecurity, pain, distress or emotional struggle)?
features.spec: Read only `argument` (OP's text). Return 1 if the OP, in their own voice, discloses a personal emotional vulnerability about themselves (e.g., admitting feeling afraid, ashamed, insecure, anxious, hurt, depressed, lonely, or emotionally struggling). Return 0 if no such disclosure exists, including purely abstract opinions, disclosures only about other people, or emotional states only in quotations from others not adopted by the OP. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome edits/updates and reports of the outcome; these are not evidence. Return null if argument is missing or malformed; empty text gives 0.

decomposed.h0: op_discloses_emotional_vulnerability has no association with the likelihood of delta (coefficient = 0).
decomposed.h1: op_discloses_emotional_vulnerability is associated with a higher likelihood of delta (coefficient > 0).
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: vulnerability is judged from the current argument text as a binary presence; no intensity scale. Argument text may include edits or outcome announcements (excluded in the semantic spec, but timing of text relative to outcome is unknown). OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model; association only, not causal.

decomposed.hypothesis: A counterargument containing specific empirical evidence is associated with a higher likelihood of the original poster awarding a delta.

features.name: any_comment_specific_empirical_evidence
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain specific empirical evidence (e.g., concrete data, statistics, studies, documented facts or cited sources) in support of its argument?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of counter-argument comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment itself offers specific empirical evidence as support: concrete statistics or numbers, named studies/research, documented historical or factual cases, or cited sources/links presented as support. Cited external sources count as evidence even though the wording is not the commenter's own. Return 0 if none do: generic reasoning, opinion, hypotheticals, vague appeals ('studies show' without any specifics) or purely personal anecdote without verifiable specifics do not count. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view or awarded a delta, post-outcome updates, and reports of the outcome; these are not evidence. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed input gives null.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_specific_empirical_evidence has no association with the likelihood of delta.
decomposed.h1: Rows with any_comment_specific_empirical_evidence=1 have a higher likelihood of delta.
decomposed.note: Assumptions: "a counterargument" is operationalized as any comment in OC_comments (any, not share or all). "Specific empirical evidence" is judged by the prompt with the criteria in the spec. Comment order, timing and per-comment outcomes are unavailable, and OC_comments may include comments after a delta was awarded, so timing is unknown. Association only, not causal. Delta announcements are excluded from the evidence judgement.

decomposed.hypothesis: Engaging with a well-reasoned counterargument correlates with a higher frequency of logical concession statements from the original poster in discussions.

features.name: has_well_reasoned_counterargument
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment present a well-reasoned counterargument (clear logic, support for its claims)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by users other than the OP). Return 1 if at least one comment gives a well-reasoned counterargument: it makes a clear, logically coherent case against the OP's view with explicit reasoning or supporting evidence. Return 0 if the list is valid but no comment does (including empty list). Return null if missing or malformed. Ignore any text announcing that the OP changed their view, delta awards, or post-outcome resolution updates as evidence. Comment order carries no meaning.

decomposed.h0: has_well_reasoned_counterargument is unrelated to the frequency of OP logical concession statements.
decomposed.h1: has_well_reasoned_counterargument is associated with a higher frequency of OP logical concession statements.
decomposed.note: The claimed outcome is frequency of logical concession statements by the OP, not the dataset outcome delta. OP concessions in the supplied text would be largely concessions/view-change announcements that reveal the outcome, and the OP's replies are not separately supplied other than within conversation, with unknown timing. No faithful measure or test with delta is available, so term=null; a delta regression would substitute a different claim. The predictor feature is provided only as a measurement of the counterargument side; well-reasoned is judged by the extractor without a supplied scale.

decomposed.hypothesis: Discussions where counter-arguments contain specific numerical data or statistics are associated with a higher likelihood of original-poster view change than those relying on general assertions.

features.name: any_comment_cites_numerical_data
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment give specific numerical data or statistics as support?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of other users' comments). Return 1 if at least one comment itself offers specific numerical data or statistics (e.g., percentages, counts, rates, measured quantities, cited study figures) as support for its argument; attributed figures from a cited source count. Return 0 if none do (only general assertions, or numbers that are not evidence such as list numbering, dates alone, or hypothetical illustrative numbers). Ignore any text announcing OP view change/delta awards or outcome reports as evidence. Empty list gives 0; missing or malformed gives null.

decomposed.h0: any_comment_cites_numerical_data has no association with the likelihood of OP view change.
decomposed.h1: Discussions with any_comment_cites_numerical_data=1 have a higher likelihood of OP view change than those without.
decomposed.note: Operational assumption: "relying on general assertions" is operationalized as no comment containing specific numerical data (any-comment presence), not as a separate measured category. Comments are unordered, with no timing; the comments may be after or contain outcome-related text, which is excluded from the measure. Association only.
